chunks: And by his chain, from Sandal, from Abi al-Subbah al-Kinani, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When it is the Night of Qadr, wherein every wise affair is made distinct, a caller will call out on that night from inside the Throne: 'Verily, Allah has forgiven whoever visited the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on this night.'

key_terms.أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ: A wise affair/command; refers to the divine decrees and matters of wisdom determined by Allah.
key_terms.بُطْنَانِ الْعَرْشِ: Inside the Throne; referring to the location from which the announcement is made, indicating proximity to the Divine.
key_terms.زَارَ: Visited; specifically refers to Ziyarah, the act of visiting the grave of the Imams or the Prophet.
key_terms.قَبْرَ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of al-Husayn; referring to the shrine of Imam al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him).
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: Night of Qadr, a night of high significance in Islam, often associated with the 19th, 21st, or 23rd of Ramadan, where divine decrees are issued.
key_terms.مُنَادٍ: A caller; a being who announces divine news.
key_terms.يُفْرَقُ: It is made distinct/separated; refers to the separation of destinies and affairs for the coming year.

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husayn's grave on Laylat al-Qadr?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, Laylat al-Qadr is viewed as the night when divine decrees are inscribed, making this specific reward for visiting Imam al-Husayn’s grave particularly significant as a means of securing forgiveness in one’s destined fate. The location of the call from beneath the Throne (Buthan al-Arsh) underscores the cosmic importance of the Ahl al-Bayt, linking the martyrdom of Husayn directly to the divine will. This narration highlights the unique spiritual status of Karbala as a locus of divine mercy and intercession.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 5. My father narrated to me from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from ‘Amraki, from Sandal, from Abil Sabbāḥ Al-Kināni, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:

On the night of Qadr, “wherein every affair of wisdom is made distinct” [44:4], a caller will call out from inside the Throne, “Verily Allāh has forgiven everyone who has come to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) on this night.”
